title: AI Training Watchdog: InfluxDB data plane

panels.title: How to demonstrate influxdb data plane

options.content:
**How InfluxDB carries the demo.** Writes go to the ingest node; trainer polls and dashboard queries go to the query node. Follow call rates, point rates, query/write latency, and the database's series and point counts.

Database panels describe all runs. **Runs**, **Run**, and the selected time range filter the control-loop panel. Series cardinality and database size count the whole database in the selected time range; they sit at the bottom because they scan every point in the range (keep it short).

panels.title: Calls per second (peak in the time range)
panels.description: Writes: successful write requests from the Flink InfluxDB connector's two sinks (telemetry, and incidents with step summaries) to the ingest node (each carries a batch of points), and points per second. Reads: control polls/s is what every trainer and simulated run reported polling (control_poll telemetry); SQL queries/s is every query the query node logged (system.queries: control polls plus this dashboard).

targets.rawSql: SELECT date_bin(INTERVAL '1 minute', time) AS time, sum(polls) / 60.0 AS "Control polls/s" FROM control_poll WHERE $__timeFilter(time) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
SELECT date_bin(INTERVAL '1 minute', issue_time) AS time, count(*) / 60.0 AS "SQL queries/s" FROM system.queries WHERE $__timeFilter(issue_time) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Latency of every call: dots are SQL queries the query node served; lines are write percentiles
panels.description: Dots: end-to-end latency of every SQL query the query node logged (system.queries, up to 10,000 kept), split into control polls (the trainers' incident queries) and dashboard queries. Lines: write latency p50 and p99 of the Flink connector's write calls to the ingest node, per minute (CloudWatch), for the telemetry sink and (dotted) the control sink, which writes the incidents; and the pollers' own p50 round trip (control_poll telemetry, client side, includes the network). Log scale.

targets.rawSql: SELECT issue_time AS time, arrow_cast(end2end_duration, 'Int64') / 1e6 AS "control poll" FROM system.queries WHERE success AND end2end_duration IS NOT NULL AND (strpos(query_text, 'AS time_ns FROM incident') > 0 AND strpos(query_text, 'system.queries') = 0) AND $__timeFilter(issue_time) ORDER BY issue_time

SELECT issue_time AS time, arrow_cast(end2end_duration, 'Int64') / 1e6 AS "dashboard query" FROM system.queries WHERE success AND end2end_duration IS NOT NULL AND NOT (strpos(query_text, 'AS time_ns FROM incident') > 0 AND strpos(query_text, 'system.queries') = 0) AND $__timeFilter(issue_time) ORDER BY issue_time
SELECT date_bin(INTERVAL '1 minute', time) AS time, median(latency_p50_ms) AS "control poll p50 (client)" FROM control_poll WHERE $__timeFilter(time) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Control loop through InfluxDB: from the triggering event to the trainer's response
panels.description: One pair of dots per command. Seen by the trainer: telemetry -> Kinesis -> Flink detects -> incident written to InfluxDB (ingest node) -> visible on the query node -> the trainer's next poll. Trainer responded: the trainer handles commands between steps, so this adds the rest of the current step (a GRPO step takes 6-8 s). A response can report an applied or ignored command; read the Incident log for the outcome.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT time, 'seen by the trainer' AS series, seen_latency_ms AS value FROM control_ack
WHERE seen_latency_ms IS NOT NULL AND $__timeFilter(time) AND $source AND run_id LIKE '${run}'
UNION ALL
SELECT time, 'trainer responded' AS series, apply_latency_ms AS value FROM control_ack
WHERE apply_latency_ms IS NOT NULL AND $__timeFilter(time) AND $source AND run_id LIKE '${run}'
ORDER BY time

defaults.noValue: No commands in the time range

panels.title: Series cardinality by measurement (selected time range)
panels.description: Distinct tag combinations per measurement in the selected time range. Per-layer and per-head statistics are widest; everything else grows with runs and ranks. Whole database: ignores the Runs and Run selectors. Heavy: it scans every point in the range, on the query node that also serves the trainers' control polls, so a wide range over millions of series slows the polls (and, at 10 million series on db.influx.medium nodes, fails).

panels.title: Database size (selected time range)
panels.description: Counted from the measurements themselves, in the selected time range: points, distinct series (tag combinations), and measurements. Whole database: ignores the Runs and Run selectors. Heavy, like Series cardinality: keep the range short.
